name: Lula Lake Land Trust
dates: First and last weekends of each month, reservations required
unique: Eight thousand protected acres on Lookout Mountain with a blue-green lake below a waterfall, opened to the public only on the first and last weekends of the month, with a trail network that connects to the Chattanooga trail system.
buzz: The waterfall and lake are the payoff and the limited weekends keep it quiet. Reservations go fast in spring, so book when the window opens.

name: Lookout Mountain Parkway
unique: A ninety three mile scenic highway along the brow of Lookout Mountain from Gadsden, Alabama to Chattanooga, running through Dade County with overlooks into the valley and pull offs at the canyon rim.
buzz: The Georgia stretch is short but the views are the best on the route. Motorcycles come up from Chattanooga on weekends.

name: Summerville Train Depot and Turntable
unique: A restored depot with a working turntable that once turned locomotives for the Chattooga line, in a town that grew where the railroad crossed the valley.
buzz: A turntable still in place is a rarity in a small town, and rail fans know it. The depot is used for events now.

name: Summerville Trade Day
dates: Every Tuesday and Saturday, year round
unique: An open air flea market on the highway that has run twice a week since 1976, with produce, tools, chickens, cast iron and whatever came out of somebody's barn that week.
buzz: Get there before seven for the good tools. It is a genuine country trade day, not a curated antique fair.

name: Greg Wyatt Vintage Corvettes Museum
unique: A dealership and museum on Commerce Street showing restored mid year Corvettes from the fifties and sixties, assembled by a man who has been doing this for forty years.
buzz: Car people call it a pilgrimage in a town nobody expects. Call first, hours depend on the owner.
